title: librarian-warm-set-time-aware-retrieval
intention: The librarian maintains a time-aware warm set so recently active context stays retrievable without re-deriving.
why: Three minds, same constraint, same shape (Akien, 2026-08-19): Akien's world is far bigger than his attention — he keeps a small handful of threads (house, CC work, medical) and his attention moves between them by rules he has internalized. CC's attention is smaller than its context — it has rules about how attention moves over surfaces and what happens when relevant things show up (memory, compression, CLAUDE.md). The librarian's world is its graph trees, and it has no attention at all — every walk treats every node equally except by cosine. The lived symptom: the librarian cannot maintain a thread across sessions, cannot prioritize what it was recently working on, and cannot wake a dormant concern when new evidence arrives. Temporal reasoning is the sharpest replicated differentiator in the field: vector-only ~31% on time-bound questions; 85% of systems failed at least half of time-related queries even when the info existed. The warm set and the temporal channel are two faces of the same thing: the librarian's attention has a WHEN, not just a WHAT.
traces_to: Telos 1 — inference compilation: the warm set is compiled readiness
Law 1 — spent on the novel: time-aware retrieval prevents re-deriving what was recently active

falsifier.proves_green: A warm-set attention architecture with event-driven thread lifecycle (wake/attend/sleep) and time-aware query expansion. Proof teeth: (1) a repeatedly co-occurring cluster of nodes crystallizes into a thread with a summary; (2) a query related to an awake thread boosts that thread's nodes in the walk; (3) a sleeping thread wakes when a new deposit touches its nodes; (4) an important recurring thread (high recurrence) does NOT decay to zero just because it hasn't been touched recently — recurrence and importance are signals alongside recency; (5) a query containing 'yesterday' filters to nodes created in the last 24 hours; (6) a pure-topic query with no temporal language and no thread relevance resolves by plain cosine — the warm set does not override; (7) the warm set updates on events only, never by daemon or timer.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) the warm set is a score multiplier only — it must be a structural set of active threads with their own lifecycle, not a dial on the walk; (2) a thread that is important and recurring (the analogue of 'medical appointments') decays to zero because it hasn't been touched recently — importance and recurrence must be signals alongside recency; (3) incoming information relevant to a dormant thread does not wake it — the warm set must route relevance, not just score it; (4) a query containing temporal language ('yesterday', 'last week', 'recently') does not expand to include a time filter; (5) the warm set requires a daemon or periodic refresh instead of updating on events (deposits, walks, resolution, promotion); (6) the warm set overrides cosine for a non-temporal pure-topic query (attention is a CHANNEL, not a replacement — the graph walk still resolves by relevance when no thread claims the question); (7) the timestamp used is ingestion time only, not event time when available (bi-temporal from ticket #2).

warm_set_table.through_db_domain: create_owned_table + read/write/update — same sole path as cairn_nodes

thread_lifecycle.wake_events: A deposit or walk touches a node in a sleeping thread → thread wakes. Detection: after deposit() or nearest() returns, check whether any result node_id appears in a sleeping thread's node_ids. An emit('resolve') with promoted nodes wakes any thread containing them. A contradiction (ticket #2) landing on a thread member wakes the thread.
thread_lifecycle.attend_events: Each resolution (resolve_query returning RESOLVED) that touches a thread's nodes: increment recurrence, update last_touched. Side effect inside _tenure_on_resolution() or _verdict().
thread_lifecycle.sleep_trigger: A thread untouched for N resolution events (not a clock — counted at each resolution) moves to sleeping. N is a dial, start at 20 resolutions. Checked as arithmetic at resolution time: last_touched older than N resolutions ago → sleep. No daemon.
thread_lifecycle.no_daemon: All lifecycle transitions fire as side effects of existing events (deposit, resolve, promote). The thread table is read and updated at the same points the tenure loop already writes — no additional process.

how.thread_creation: When a cluster of nodes appears together in resolution walks more than M times (measured by link traversals or co-occurrence counting via cairn_links traversals column) and does not belong to an existing thread, a new thread crystallizes. Inference (resolve kind='generate') supplies the summary from the cluster's contents. The thread enters at 'awake'. M is a dial, start at 3 co-occurrences.
how.warm_boost: nearest() gains an optional threads parameter (list of awake thread dicts). For each walked node, if the node belongs to an awake thread whose summary cosine to the query exceeds a threshold (0.5), the node's similarity score gets an additive boost (0.1). The boost is ADDITIVE, not multiplicative — a non-thread node at cosine 0.8 still beats a thread node at 0.5+0.1. This satisfies falsifier (6): the graph walk still resolves by relevance when no thread claims the question.

temporal_expansion.detection: Parse temporal language in the question using simple pattern matching: 'yesterday', 'last week', 'last month', 'recently' (= last 7 days), 'today', ISO date patterns, 'N days ago'. No inference needed — temporal language is syntactically regular.
temporal_expansion.mechanism: When temporal language is detected, compute a time window (start_ts, end_ts). Pre-filter the leaf rows to nodes whose created timestamp falls within the window BEFORE the cosine walk. If the filtered set has fewer than k nodes, widen the window by 2x and note the widening in the verdict.
temporal_expansion.bi_temporal: When ticket #2's invalidation timestamps land, expand to support event_time vs ingestion_time queries. Until then, created (ingestion time) is the only timestamp available.
temporal_expansion.integration: A pre-processing step in resolve_query() before the first nearest() call. The temporal filter is applied to the leaf rows, not to the query vector — it narrows WHAT is walked, not HOW the walk scores.

how.size_bound: The warm set is bounded at 7 threads (Akien's handful). When an 8th thread would crystallize, the lowest-importance sleeping thread is retired (removed from cairn_threads, its nodes stay in the graph). If all 7 are awake, the least-recurrent one sleeps to make room. The bound is a dial.

integration_points.deposit: After deposit(), check for thread wake events.
integration_points.resolve_query: Before nearest(), apply temporal expansion. After nearest(), apply warm_boost. After _tenure_on_resolution(), fire thread attend/sleep/creation events.
integration_points.nearest: The warm_boost parameter is optional — callers outside the loop use plain cosine.
integration_points.emit_events: The existing emit('deposit') and emit('resolve') events carry all the data thread lifecycle needs — no new events required.
